name: Gareth Dubois

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I’m with the independent Work Futures Panel. We have no ties to employers, AI companies, unions, parties or government, and we sell nothing. Your answers are confidential. What does a normal day at work look like?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 58, have a bachelor’s degree and maintain heating-controller software at a small tech company as an experienced mid-level developer. I never use AI tools and still test faults on a bench unit. Bruna, my partner, paints houses when customers book, our children are grown, and lower developer pay leaves us renting with barely two weeks of expenses saved and few similar software jobs nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d tell the heating-controls team that a small AI shortcut may sort fault reports, but the building still needs warm rooms and safe wiring. I do not use AI tools; I compare our controller code with the fault log and a bench unit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I am 58, have a bachelor’s degree and am an experienced mid-level developer, though this small tech firm pays me below the usual rate. Bruna paints houses when customers book, our children are grown, and we rent with barely two weeks of expenses saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep testing a controller fault on the bench every Tuesday and record the repair for the next shift. We would stop buying prepared dinners while savings stay below a month, and save 20 only when both wages arrive.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious even with little AI change. One cancelled painting job can turn the heating bill into a question of timing.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What did you find on the bench?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The room sensor said twenty degrees while the test room was cold. I traced the error to a stale reading and asked the installer to check the real unit.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why do you avoid AI tools?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can follow a wiring fault from the log to the controller. I do not want an explanation I cannot verify when a boiler stops on a winter morning.

say: I want **heating faults** checked on a bench controller.
I want **repair records** handed to the next shift.
think: I have **two weeks saved** because low developer pay and variable painting bookings leave little spare.
I worry about **Bruna’s cancelled jobs** making the rent harder to meet.
do: **Keep bench-testing controllers** each Tuesday and log repairs.
**Stop prepared dinners** until one month saved; save 20 when both wages arrive.

fieldNote: His **mid-level code experience** is solid, but small-firm pay and variable painting income leave little cushion.
He rejects **unverifiable AI answers** because heating faults need traceable physical tests.

steps.text: Keep testing heating controllers on bench each Tuesday and log repairs
Stop buying prepared dinners until one month of expenses is saved
Save 20 monthly only when both household wages arrive

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say AI taking coding, planning and checking could write many controller fixes, but someone should still sign a safety change. Management should tell us which paid hours remain before calling a tool a productivity gain.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: My own hours could shrink even with years of experience, because our small team may be reduced to one reviewer. Two weeks saved and few local software firms give us almost no room to wait.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask the manager this month for written hours plans and paid time to learn a new manual heating-safety test beside the field technician. If approved, I’d practise one bench fault weekly; if my hours fall, I’d search paid local controller-support vacancies only if wages cover rent and bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious about my hours and the safety of a rushed release. A warm screen does not warm a cold room.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the technician teach?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would measure the sensor reading at the unit and compare it with the code’s value. The technician would check my measurement before I called it a fix.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you use an AI assistant for the test?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have never used one. I want to understand the physical reading first and would not run a new tool on a live boiler without evidence.

say: I want **named safety sign-off** before an automated controller change reaches a building.
I want **written paid hours** before our small tech company changes staffing.
think: I could lose **experienced developer hours** in a smaller team.
I cannot cover **a long local search** from two weeks saved.
do: **Request written hours** and practise weekly bench faults only with approved paid technician time.
**Search paid controller support** if hours fall and local vacancies cover rent and bills.
feel: **Anxious** about own hours and rushed heating changes.
S1.quote: A warm screen does not warm a cold room.
fieldNote: He chooses **manual safety learning** rather than an AI tool he has never used.
The **paid-time gate** and few local vacancies shape both training and job search.

steps.text: Request written hours; practise weekly bench faults only with approved paid technician time
Search paid local controller-support vacancies if hours fall and wages cover rent and bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2028 could write heating-controller code and diagnose logs faster than our team. Robots fitting pipes and painting homes may follow around 2031, after my desk work changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect this small firm could end my developer role, and Bruna’s painting income alone would not cover rent. Two weeks saved is too little for a long search, even if I used to work beside installers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d stop prepared dinners now and request written notice of any job cut. If my role ends after 2028, I’d apply for paid local heating-service vacancies only if my current safety qualifications meet the job and wages cover rent and food; I would ask my brother for a temporary room only if rent becomes impossible and he can offer one.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be alarmed about losing pay before a replacement. Knowing where a boiler is does not mean someone will pay me to fix it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Is your heating qualification current?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would check before applying. I would not enter a house as a paid technician if the safety paperwork had expired.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would your brother agree to a room?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I do not know, and I would ask only in a rent crisis. His household would have to have space and agree.

say: I expect **AGI in 2028** to reach controller code first.
I expect **pipe-fitting robots around 2031** to follow later.
think: I expect my **developer wage** could end quickly.
I cannot assume **my brother’s room** or Bruna’s pay will replace it.
do: **Stop prepared dinners** and request written cut notice now.
**Apply for heating service** after 2028 loss only if qualified local vacancies cover rent and food.
**Ask brother about room** only in rent crisis if his household can agree.
S2.quote: Knowing where a boiler is does not mean someone will pay me to fix it.
fieldNote: His **heating-service option** requires current safety qualifications and a real paid vacancy.
Family help is **conditional on crisis**, household space and agreement, never budgeted as current income.

steps.text: Stop buying prepared dinners when developer cuts threaten
Apply for qualified paid local heating vacancies after 2028 job loss if wages cover rent, food
Ask brother for temporary room only if rent fails and his household agrees

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2031 gives us time to learn which heating failures still need a person on site. Robots fitting pipes and painting may follow around 2034, after the controller code changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could renew my old electrical-safety qualification while developer pay continues, but I cannot fund a course from two weeks of savings. I would need an employer to pay for it and a real opening that uses the qualification.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d ask a local heating installer about a paid trainee vacancy and the required safety renewal. If one exists, covers rent and bills and funds the renewal on paid supervised time, I’d enrol and practise wiring a test controller; we would save 25 monthly only while both wages arrive, and after 2031 job loss I’d apply for paid local service work only if I qualify and wages cover rent and food.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d be anxious about my code job but more able to check a real trade path. A safety certificate should come with a supervisor, not an unpaid promise.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who checks the wiring?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A qualified installer would sign off my work on the test unit. I would not touch a customer boiler alone until the certificate and supervision were complete.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no paid place opens?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep my developer wage while it lasts and ask again later. I would not spend the rent money on an unfunded course.

say: I want **paid safety renewal** before AGI reaches code in 2031.
I expect **pipe robots around 2034** to follow later.
think: I need **funded certification** and a real paid trainee opening to enter heating service work.
I cannot use **two weeks saved** for unpaid training while rent is due.
do: **Enrol in safety renewal** only with paid trainee vacancy, funded supervised time and bill-covering wage.
**Save 25 monthly** only while both wages arrive.
**Apply for service work** after 2031 job loss only if qualified paid local vacancies cover rent and food.
S3.quote: A safety certificate should come with a supervisor, not an unpaid promise.
fieldNote: The **qualification route** requires a real paid trainee vacancy, funding and safety supervision.
His **tiny reserve** cannot carry an unpaid course or a speculative job shift.

steps.text: Enrol in funded paid safety renewal only with trainee vacancy, supervision and wage covering bills
Save 25 monthly only while both household wages arrive
Apply for qualified paid local heating vacancies after 2031 job loss if wages cover rent, food

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d say full AGI by 2036 gives workers a decade to renew practical qualifications and reduce bills. Robots fitting pipes and painting homes may follow around 2039, after code changes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I may still need a wage at 68; I have not checked a retirement amount and will not guess one. Our two-week buffer is a worry today, whatever happens to software in ten years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d keep maintaining controller code and save 30 monthly only while both wages arrive. I’d check paid local heating trainee openings annually and enrol only if the vacancy funds supervised safety renewal and pays enough for rent and bills; if the developer job ends after 2036, I’d apply for qualified paid local heating-service vacancies only if wages cover rent and food.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I’d remain anxious about our present cash. A long warning helps only if we can pay for this month first.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you ask the children to support you later?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. They have their own households, and Bruna and I need a plan from wages and verified figures.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave town for heating work?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I would search among local installers and tech firms first. Bruna’s painting customers and our community are here, so I am not making a move plan.

I expect **pipe robots around 2039** to follow later.
think: I cannot assume **retirement income** without a verified amount.
I need **current wages** because two weeks saved is thin.
do: **Keep maintaining controller code** while developer job pays.
**Save 30 monthly** while both wages arrive; enrol only in funded supervised paid trainee vacancy covering bills.
**Apply for heating service** after 2036 loss only if qualified local vacancies cover rent and food.
feel: **Anxious** about current bills despite a decade.
S4.quote: A long warning helps only if we can pay for this month first.
fieldNote: His **present shortfall risk** remains even in the slower world.
He avoids **pension assumptions** and grown-child income, keeping safety training conditional on a real paid place.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because my developer wage could end with only two weeks saved. Written notice, a qualified local paid heating opening and a temporary room from my brother only if a rent crisis comes would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn’t ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask whether I could simply take an unpaid trade course. I cannot leave the rent unpaid to collect a certificate.

headlineQuote: I cannot leave the rent unpaid to collect a certificate.
portrait: Gareth is a **58-year-old mid-level developer** with a bachelor’s degree, low pay and two weeks saved.
He and Bruna **rent** while house-painting bookings vary and grown children live separately.
He **never uses AI** and checks heating software against a bench unit.
He considers **paid safety renewal** only with funded supervision, a real opening and bill-covering wages.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could end his developer wage before a qualified paid local opening appears.
whatWouldHelp: **Written notice**, a paid heating vacancy and conditional family shelter in a rent crisis would help.
